title: CiteVQA: Benchmarking Evidence Attribution for Trustworthy Document Intelligence
research_question: How can document visual question answering be evaluated so that a model receives credit only when its answer is correct and its cited document region genuinely supports that answer?
methodology: CiteVQA constructs a benchmark of 1,897 questions over 711 PDFs spanning seven domains and two languages, including single-document and multi-document settings. Its automated construction pipeline parses documents, links related documents, extracts evidence packages, generates and verifies question-answer pairs, and uses masking ablation to identify crucial evidence before expert review. Gold evidence is represented at element-level bounding-box granularity with document and page indices, and synthetic multi-document evidence is mapped back to coordinates in the original source PDFs. Twenty multimodal language models are evaluated using evidence recall, relevance, answer correctness, page-level metrics, and Strict Attributed Accuracy, which jointly requires acceptable answers and evidence.

key_findings.finding: CiteVQA demonstrates a substantial gap between answer correctness and faithful evidence attribution: the strongest evaluated system reports 76.0 Strict Attributed Accuracy despite an 86.1 answer score, while the strongest open-source model reports 22.5 SAA.

Evidence attribution becomes more difficult as document scope increases; for the strongest system, reported evidence recall decreases from 68.9 in the single-document setting to 55.3 in the multi-document multiple-gold setting.
key_findings.section: §4 Main Results and Appendix analysis of multi-document complexity

key_findings.finding: Restricting models to ground-truth pages or gold documents improves answer accuracy in the paper's oracle-style analyses, providing preliminary evidence that evidence localization is itself an important performance bottleneck rather than merely an explanation layer.

The benchmark provides a hierarchical spatial evidence address consisting of document index, page index, and element bounding box, and its multi-document synthesis pipeline maintains a mapping from synthetic evidence back to source-PDF coordinates.
key_findings.section: §4.1 Evaluation Metrics and §8.1 Spatial Mapping and Evidence Synthesis

key_findings.finding: A human study on a sampled subset finds no statistically significant difference between the automated and human assessments for the reported relevance and answer-correctness judging dimensions, supporting the evaluation pipeline's use of automated judges.
key_findings.section: §9.2 Validation of Automated Evaluation via Human Study

limitations: CiteVQA grounds evidence in static PDF coordinates and does not define stable region identifiers or lineage across successive revisions of the same PDF.
Document index, page index, and bounding-box coordinates can change after pagination, layout, or content revisions, so they are not by themselves revision-stable identifiers.
The automated annotation pipeline relies on capable document parsers and MLLMs and is computationally expensive to reproduce at full scale.
The paper notes that determining authoritative evidence can be domain-dependent even when a visually matching region is available.
Evaluation uses model-based relevance and correctness judges, adding cost and another possible source of error despite the reported human validation.
The benchmark distribution may encourage overfitting if systems are tuned closely to its domains and document characteristics.
Benchmark annotations and code are available, but access to the complete source-PDF collection is constrained by copyright and may require approval or rely on external URLs.
raw_claims: CiteVQA contains 1,897 questions derived from 711 multi-page PDFs across seven broad domains and two languages.
Each gold citation identifies evidence at element-level bounding-box granularity rather than only at page level.
Strict Attributed Accuracy requires both the answer and the supporting evidence to satisfy the benchmark's correctness criteria.
Models can produce correct textual answers while citing incorrect document regions.
The benchmark includes single-document, multi-document one-gold, and multi-document multiple-gold scenarios.
Masking candidate evidence elements is used during dataset construction to help identify evidence that is crucial for answering a question.
Synthetic multi-document evidence is mapped back to the spatial coordinates of its original source document.
The released repository contains inference, evaluation, summarization, prompts, and benchmark-data tooling.
Oracle-style restriction to correct pages or documents improves answer accuracy for several evaluated models.
CiteVQA does not track the identity of a document element across revised versions of the same attachment.
